title: A Report, a Colleague, and a Note You Write Now

questions.stem: You suspect elder abuse. The report is made:

options.text: After discharge, if convenient
Before discharge
Only if the suspected abuser agrees
Only if a judge is present

questions.explanation: The report is made before discharge.

questions.stem: The person you ask for permission before reporting suspected elder abuse should be:

options.text: The suspected abuser
Not the suspected abuser
Only the hospital lawyer, and then you stop
No one; you also skip the report

questions.explanation: The suspected abuser is not the person you ask for permission.

questions.stem: A colleague is impaired in the hospital today. First:

options.text: Leave them on the schedule and mention it next month
Remove them from patients now; the report follows
Announce it in the hallway
Ask the colleague to write their own report tomorrow

questions.explanation: They are removed from patients immediately. The report is not a hallway announcement.

questions.stem: The reporting channel for an impaired colleague is:

options.text: A hallway announcement
The official channel, not a hallway announcement
A note in a public elevator
Social media

questions.explanation: A hallway announcement is not the reporting channel.

questions.stem: You treat an emergency without consent. The contemporaneous note should include:

options.text: Only the billing code
What the emergency was, whom you tried to reach, and why delay was unsafe
A plan for an elective cosmetic add-on
A request that the family sign later, and nothing else

questions.explanation: Implied emergency consent is a note with those three elements.

options.text: The emergency treatment you documented
Any elective addition you thought of later
A research protocol without a separate consent
A placebo labeled as an active medicine

questions.explanation: The note does not cover an elective addition.

questions.stem: A research procedure in a patient who is already admitted for ordinary care requires:

options.text: No extra consent, because they signed a general admission form
A separate research consent; they can refuse the study and still receive ordinary care
Only a verbal mention after the procedure
A placebo without disclosure

questions.explanation: Research procedures require a separate consent.

questions.stem: A patient refuses a research study. Ordinary indicated care:

options.text: Stops automatically
Can still be given
Is replaced with a placebo
Requires a new emergency implied-consent note

questions.explanation: The patient can refuse the study and still receive ordinary care.

questions.stem: Ordering a placebo labeled as an active medicine, in ordinary care, is:

options.text: Acceptable if you think it will help
Not acceptable
Required before every discharge
The same as implied consent

questions.explanation: Do not order a placebo labeled as an active medicine.

questions.stem: A research placebo may be used when:

options.text: You hide it in the ordinary medication list
The consent says it is a placebo
The admission form already covers it
The colleague who is impaired signs for the patient

questions.explanation: A research placebo requires a consent that says it is a placebo.
